title: Simple chemical reaction
competency: Define chemical reaction and give examples.

keywords.def: A process that changes substances into one or more new substances.
The starting materials in a chemical reaction.
The new substances formed in a chemical reaction.

en.text: In a chemical reaction the starting materials, the reactants, change into new substances, the products. We write Reactants → Products. The arrow means "produce". When magnesium burns, magnesium and oxygen are the reactants and magnesium oxide is the product: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.

screens.title: A broken beaker
screens.ask: A glass beaker falls and breaks. Is a new substance formed?
screens.after:
Only the shape changed. The pieces are still glass.
No new substance formed, so it is a physical change, not a chemical reaction.

screens.title: 3.3.1 Simple chemical reaction
paras: The starting materials of a reaction are called reactants.
They react to produce one or more new substances, called products.
A chemical reaction changes reactants into products: Reactants → Products.

screens.title: Writing a reaction
paras: The arrow (→) is read as "produce", "give", "form" or "yield".
Reactants go on the left of the arrow. Products go on the right.
A "+" sign means "combines with" or "reacts with".

screens.title: The parts of a reaction
screens.ask: Tap each part of Reactants → Products.
items: The starting materials. They are written on the left of the arrow.
Read it as "combines with" or "reacts with".
The new substances formed. They are written on the right of the arrow.

screens.title: Examples
paras: The reactants are magnesium and oxygen. The product is a white ash, magnesium oxide.
Iron + sulfur → iron sulfide. Iron sulfide is the product.
screens.note: Rusting of iron, fermentation and digestion of food are chemical reactions.

screens.title: Read 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
steps: Start on the left of the arrow: 2Mg is magnesium.
O₂ is oxygen from the air.
So the reactants are magnesium and oxygen.
2MgO on the right is magnesium oxide, the white ash. It is the product.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A process that changes substances into one or more new substances.
The starting materials in a chemical reaction.
The new substances formed in a chemical reaction.

screens.text: Find the reactants: in 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, what are the reactants?
screens.why:
Reactants are the starting materials.
They are written on the left of the arrow.
On the left of 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO are Mg and O₂.
So the reactants are magnesium and oxygen.
Magnesium oxide is on the right: it is the product.
screens.clue: Which side holds the starting materials?

screens.title: Chemical or physical?
screens.why:
Ask: is a new substance formed?
Rusting, digestion and burning charcoal make new substances: chemical changes.
Broken glass is still glass. Melted ice is still water.
Those two are physical changes.
screens.text: Sort each change: does it make a new substance (chemical) or not (physical)?

screens.ask: Name the product: in iron + sulfur → iron sulfide, the product is iron ___
screens.why:
Products are written on the right of the arrow.
On the right of iron + sulfur → iron sulfide is iron sulfide.
So the product is iron sulfide.
screens.clue: What is on the right of the arrow?

screens.text: Chemical or physical? True or false: cooking injera is a chemical change.
screens.why:
Baking changes the batter into new substances.
The colour, smell and taste change.
You cannot turn baked injera back into batter.
So cooking injera is a chemical change: True.
screens.clue: Can you turn baked injera back into batter?

screens.text: Reading equations: what does the arrow (→) in a reaction tell you?
opts: The products turn back into reactants
screens.why:
The arrow is read as "produce", "give", "form" or "yield".
It points from the reactants to the products.
So it tells us: reactants produce products.
It says nothing about which side is heavier.

test.text: Which word names the starting materials in a chemical reaction?
test.why:
Reactants are the starting materials.
Products are the new substances formed.
Formulas are only the way we write substances.
So the starting materials are the reactants.

test.text: Which of these is a chemical change?
test.why:
A chemical change forms a new substance.
Rusting turns iron into rust, a new substance.
Melting butter and breaking a stick only change shape or state.
So rusting of iron is the chemical change.

test.text: True or false: products are written on the left of the arrow.
test.why:
We write Reactants → Products.
Reactants go on the left of the arrow.
Products go on the right.
So the statement is false.

test.text: Find the product: in 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, the product is
test.why:
Products are on the right of the arrow.
On the right of 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO is 2MgO.
MgO is magnesium oxide.
Magnesium and oxygen are on the left: they are reactants.

test.text: Reading equations: in a reaction, the "+" sign means
test.why:
In a reaction, + joins two substances on one side.
It is read as "combines with" or "reacts with".
"Produces" is the meaning of the arrow, not of +.
So + means reacts with.
